mainTopic: A series of בעיות: swallowed palm leaves and טומאה, wheat from the clouds for the שתי הלחם, and whether original or added growth decides for the עומר and for מעשר.
overview: This עמוד is a string of questions (בעיות). First, the גמרא finishes asking whether palm leaves that an elephant swallowed and passed count as 'digested', so that a basket made from them is like כלי גללים, which cannot become טמא. A proof from children swallowed by wolves, whose flesh was declared טהור and bones טמא, is pushed off both ways: flesh is softer than palm leaves, and bones are harder. Next, רבי זירא asks whether wheat that fell from the clouds may be used for the שתי הלחם, since the פסוק says ממושבתיכם. The גמרא shows that such a thing really happened, to עדי טייעא. Then רבי שמעון בן פזי asks about a stalk that reached a third of its growth before the עומר and was replanted after it: do we follow the original growth or the added growth? Proofs from a grafted ערלה vine and an onion in a vineyard are rejected, because they may only show that we follow the original part to be strict. That question ends in תיקו. Finally, רבה asks the same kind of question about מעשר, and the case is spelled out on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Is the swallowed material now like dung vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes asking whether material that passed through an animal's digestive tract counts as digested, so that a vessel made from it is like כלי גללים, which cannot become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it like dung vessels and earth vessels, which cannot become impure? As the Master said: stone vessels, dung vessels and earth vessels cannot become impure, neither by תורה law nor by rabbinic law. Or maybe this does not count as digestion?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a two-sided question: does a basket made from palm leaves that an elephant swallowed and passed count as a 'dung vessel', or not?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the leaves count as digested, they are now just animal waste. A vessel made from them would then be like כלי גללים, which can never become טמא. If they are not considered digested, they are still ordinary plant material, and the basket can become טמא like any regular vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels made of dried animal dung
Rabbinic law, as opposed to Torah law
Digestion: the food has been broken down inside the body

steps.confusionAlert: This line begins in the middle of the question. The case itself (palm leaves swallowed by an elephant and made into a basket) was set up just before this point.

phrases.english: like dung vessels, like earth vessels,
and they are not susceptible to ritual impurity –
as the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלֵי אֲבָנִים וּכְלֵי גְלָלִים וּכְלֵי אֲדָמָה
phrases.english: Stone vessels, dung vessels, and earth vessels
are not susceptible to ritual impurity,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וְלֹא מִדִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים,
phrases.english: neither by Torah law nor by rabbinic law;
or perhaps it is not considered digestion?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a בעיא that was introduced before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does passage through an animal's digestive system count as עיכול, turning the material into dung for the laws of טומאה?

steps.title: Proof attempt from the children swallowed by wolves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer from a case where wolves swallowed two children: the חכמים ruled that the flesh was טהור, which suggests that swallowed material counts as digested.
steps.simpleTranslation: Resolve it from what עולא said in the name of רבי שמעון בר יהוצדק: once wolves swallowed two children on the other side of the Jordan. The case came before the חכמים, and they declared the flesh pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case to try to answer the question: human flesh that passed through wolves was declared טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A human body normally carries very strong טומאה. If the חכמים still declared the flesh טהור, it must have lost its status as human flesh by being digested. The same should be true of the palm leaves, so the basket would count as a dung vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: The other (eastern) side of the Jordan River

phrases.english: Resolve it from this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר עוּלָּא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: that Ulla said in the name of Rabbi Shimon bar Yehotzadak:
There was an incident where wolves swallowed two children
on the other side of the Jordan,
and the incident came before the Sages,
and they declared the flesh pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to resolve the question from step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That swallowed material counts as digested (עיכול).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling reported by עולא in the name of רבי שמעון בר יהוצדק: the flesh of children swallowed by wolves was declared טהור.

steps.title: Flesh is soft, so it is different
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: flesh is soft and digests easily, but palm leaves are tough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Flesh is different, because it is soft.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by pointing to a difference between flesh and palm leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soft flesh really does break down in the stomach, so it is fair to call it digested. Tough palm leaves may come out mostly whole. So the ruling about flesh does not tell us anything about the leaves.

phrases.english: Flesh is different, because it is soft.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the comparison from flesh to palm leaves.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Flesh is soft and easily digested; palm leaves are hard, so the cases are not alike.

steps.title: Proof the other way from the bones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove the opposite from the end of the same ruling: the bones were declared טמא, so hard things are not considered digested.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us resolve it from the end of that case: they declared the bones impure!
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same story, the גמרא now tries to prove the other side of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If hardness is what matters, the bones show that hard things are not counted as digested. Palm leaves are also hard. So the basket should be like any regular vessel and able to become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a statement or ruling

phrases.english: But let us resolve it from the last part:
and they declared the bones impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the point of step 3 (hardness matters) and uses it to prove the opposite side.
steps.raayaObject: That hard swallowed material is not considered digested, so the basket can become טמא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the same ruling: the bones were declared טמא.

steps.title: Bones are harder still
steps.stepSummary: This proof is rejected too: bones are much harder than palm leaves, so they cannot teach us about the leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bones are different, because they are much harder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof as well, so the question about the palm leaves stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Palm leaves fall in between: harder than flesh but softer than bones. Neither half of the wolves ruling covers them. So the original question remains open.
steps.whatToRemember: Palm leaves sit between flesh (soft, counts as digested) and bones (very hard, not digested). That is why neither half of the wolves case settles the question.

phrases.english: Bones are different, because they are much harder.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the comparison from bones to palm leaves.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Bones are much harder than palm leaves, so the cases are not alike.

steps.title: רבי זירא asks about wheat from the clouds
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא raises a new question: what is the law of wheat that fell from the clouds?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: wheat that came down in the clouds, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי זירא asks about wheat that fell from the sky, but he does not yet say which law he is asking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is unclear as it stands, because wheat matters for many different laws. That is why the גמרא will next ask what exactly he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks / raises a question he cannot resolve

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
Wheat that came down in the clouds, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the swallowed palm leaves.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the halachic status of wheat that fell from the clouds?

steps.title: Which law is the question about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which law רבי זירא meant, and rules out ordinary מנחות, since there is no reason this wheat would be unfit for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what purpose? If for meal offerings, why not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי זירא's question is really about, and immediately rules out one possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary מנחות can be brought from wheat grown anywhere. So wheat from the clouds would clearly be fine for them, and there would be nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: For what purpose? (Which law is being asked about?)
Why not? (Of course it is fine)

phrases.english: For what purpose?
If for meal offerings – why not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the scope of רבי זירא's question in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which halachic issue does רבי זירא's question concern?

steps.title: The question is about the שתי הלחם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי זירא is asking whether this wheat may be used for the שתי הלחם of שבועות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question is about the two loaves: what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles what the question is about: the שתי הלחם, the special offering of two loaves on שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שתי הלחם have stricter requirements about where their wheat comes from than ordinary מנחות. So it is a real question whether wheat that fell from the clouds qualifies. The question itself is now clearly defined, but not yet answered.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering of two wheat loaves brought on שבועות

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common pattern in the גמרא: before answering a question, the גמרא first pins down exactly which law is being asked about.

phrases.english: Rather, for the two loaves, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clarifying question of step 7 by narrowing the case to the שתי הלחם.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי זירא's question is about whether wheat from the clouds may be used for the שתי הלחם.

steps.title: The two ways to read 'from your dwellings'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out both sides of רבי זירא's question: does ממושבתיכם only exclude wheat from חוצה לארץ, or does it demand wheat from ארץ ישראל only?
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה said 'from your dwellings.' Maybe that only comes to exclude wheat from outside the Land, but wheat from the clouds is fine. Or maybe 'from your dwellings' is meant exactly, so even wheat from the clouds is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two possible sides of רבי זירא's question about using cloud-wheat for the שתי הלחם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on how to read the word ממושבתיכם. If it is only a negative rule that pushes out חוצה לארץ wheat, then cloud-wheat, which is not from חוצה לארץ, is fine. If it is a positive rule that the wheat must come from the Land itself, then cloud-wheat fails because it did not grow there.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From your dwellings', the word in the פסוק about the שתי הלחם

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether cloud-wheat counts as חוצה לארץ. Everyone agrees it does not. The question is whether the פסוק only rules out חוצה לארץ, or whether it demands wheat that actually grew in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said, "From your dwellings"
to exclude wheat from outside the Land, that it is not fit,
but wheat from the clouds is fine;
or perhaps "from your dwellings" is meant exactly,
and so even wheat from the clouds is also not fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״מִמּוֹשְׁבֹתֵיכֶם״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, לְאַפּוֹקֵי דְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the two sides of the question identified in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does ממושבתיכם only exclude חוצה לארץ wheat, or does it require wheat grown in ארץ ישראל?

steps.title: Can wheat really fall from the clouds?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether such a case could ever really happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is there really such a thing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check whether the case in רבי זירא's question is realistic at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A question about an impossible case would be pointless. So before going further, the גמרא wants to know if wheat ever falls from the sky.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this, a case of this kind

phrases.english: But is there really a case like this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the case raised in steps 6-9 can actually happen.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does wheat ever actually fall from the clouds?

steps.title: Yes: the story of עדי טייעא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it did happen: wheat rained down on עדי טייעא, a handbreadth high over three פרסאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, like what happened to עדי the Arab: wheat came down on him a handbreadth high, across three parasangs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes and brings a real event where wheat fell from the sky.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows the case is real, so רבי זירא's question has a practical point. The גמרא gives no answer to the question itself here, so it stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, a measure of height
Parasangs, a long measure of distance

phrases.english: Yes, as in the case of עדי the Arab,
wheat came down on him a handbreadth high
over three parasangs.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, it really happened to עדי טייעא.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא's question is real, not imaginary, but the גמרא leaves it unanswered.

steps.title: A stalk replanted after the עומר: original growth or added growth?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן פזי asks about a stalk that reached a third before the עומר, was uprooted and replanted after it, and grew more. Do we follow the original part, which the עומר made permitted, or the new growth?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן פזי asked: a stalk reached a third of its growth before the עומר. Then someone pulled it up and replanted it after the עומר, and it grew more. What is the law? Do we follow the main original part, so the עומר made it permitted? Or do we follow the added growth, so it stays forbidden until next year's עומר?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבי שמעון בן פזי asks whether growth added after the עומר follows the earlier growth that was already permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain that reached a third of its growth before the עומר becomes permitted by that עומר. Here the stalk was already permitted, but after replanting it gained new growth that the עומר never covered. The question is which part decides the status of the whole stalk.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering on the second day of פסח that permits the new grain
We go after..., meaning which factor decides

phrases.english: רבי שמעון בן פזי asked:
A stalk that reached a third of its growth before the עומר,
and someone uprooted it and replanted it after the עומר,
and it grew more: what is the law?
Do we follow the original part, and the עומר permitted it,
phrases.notes: Since it reached a third before the עומר, that עומר already made it permitted.

phrases.english: or perhaps we follow the added growth,
and it is forbidden until the next עומר comes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, unrelated question about the עומר permitting new grain.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does growth added after the עומר follow the original permitted growth, or is it judged on its own?

steps.title: A try to answer from a young vine grafted onto an old one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests solving the question from רבי יוחנן: a young vine with fruit grafted onto an old vine stays forbidden, even if the growth grows two hundred times larger. So we follow the original part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Solve it from what רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a young vine that was grafted onto an old one, while it had fruit on it, stays forbidden even if the fruit grew two hundred times more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבי שמעון בן פזי's question from a ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The young vine's fruit is forbidden as ערלה. Normally a forbidden part can be cancelled by two hundred permitted parts, but here the new growth does not cancel it. That shows the added growth follows the original part, so in our case the stalk should follow its original, permitted growth.

keyTerms.meaning: A young vine, still under three years old
An old vine, past the years of ערלה
Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: In רבי יוחנן's case the original part is forbidden, while in our case the original part is permitted. The proof is not about permitted or forbidden. It shows that the added growth follows the original growth, whatever that is.

phrases.english: Resolve it from this,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: which רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
A young vine that someone grafted onto an old one,
and it had fruit on it,
even if it grew two hundred times more, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מֵהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.raayaObject: That the added growth follows the original part (בתר עיקר אזלינן).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן about a young vine grafted onto an old one.

steps.title: Second proof: an onion planted in a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן rules that an onion planted in a vineyard stays forbidden even after the vineyard is uprooted and the onion grows two hundred times more. This suggests again that we follow the original part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: if someone planted an onion in a vineyard, and later the vineyard was uprooted, the onion is still forbidden, even if it grew two hundred times bigger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case to back up the idea from Step 13 that we follow the original part of the plant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The onion first grew while the vineyard stood, so that part was forbidden as כלאי הכרם. Most of its later growth came after the vineyard was gone, yet the whole onion stays forbidden. So the original part decides, just like the grafted vine in Step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Grew two hundred times more than its original size

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
An onion that someone planted in a vineyard,
and then the vineyard was uprooted,
even if the onion grew two hundred times more, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel proof to the grafted-vine proof of Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון בן פזי's question (Step 12): do we follow the original part or the new growth?
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יונתן's ruling that an onion from a vineyard stays forbidden despite two-hundredfold new growth.

steps.title: The proofs only show strictness, and that is the real question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects both proofs. They follow the original part only to be strict, but the open question is whether we also follow it to be lenient, as in the עומר case.
steps.simpleTranslation: That itself is what he is asking: Is it fully clear to the רבנן that we follow the original part, no matter whether that makes things easier or stricter? Or maybe they are unsure, so they follow the original part to be strict, but not to be lenient?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the two proofs. It says they don't answer the question, because the question itself is about this exact point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the vine and onion cases, following the original part makes the food forbidden, which is strict. In the עומר case, following the original part would make the new growth permitted, which is lenient. Maybe the רבנן are only unsure, and when unsure we are strict, so the proofs say nothing about a lenient case.

keyTerms.meaning: That itself is what he is asking (your proof is the very question)
The original, main part of the plant

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the עומר case is the strict one. There, following the original part is what lets you eat the new growth, so it is the lenient side.

phrases.english: That itself is what he is asking about:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי שמעון בן פזי, who asked the question in Step 12.

phrases.english: Is it completely clear to the Rabbis
that we follow the original part,

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא לְקוּלָּא וְלָא שְׁנָא לְחוּמְרָא?
phrases.english: no matter whether it leads to leniency or to strictness?
Or maybe they are unsure about it,
and so to be strict we say it,
but to be lenient we do not say it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proofs of Steps 13 and 14 by showing they cover only the strict side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both proofs: the grafted vine (Step 13) and the onion in the vineyard (Step 14).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both cases follow the original part only to be strict. That may come from doubt, so it cannot prove we follow it to be lenient, as the עומר case would need.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רבי שמעון בן פזי's question with תיקו: it remains unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the proofs pushed away, there is no source that settles whether the original part decides in a lenient case. So the question about the replanted stalk after the עומר is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: We follow the original part to be strict (ערלה, כלאי הכרם). Whether we also follow it to be lenient, as with new growth after the עומר, stays a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question after the proofs were rejected in Step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון בן פזי's question about a stalk replanted after the עומר remains unresolved.

steps.title: רבה asks how this works for tithes
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks a new, related question: what is the law about such growth when it comes to מעשר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה asked: what is the law regarding tithes?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה opens a new question that uses the same idea of original part versus new growth, this time for מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from the עומר to the duty to tithe produce. The question is still whether the original part or the new growth decides the plant's status, but now for a different law.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithe, the tenth of produce that must be separated

phrases.english: Rabba asked: regarding tithes, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same idea as Step 12 (original part versus new growth) for a new area of law, מעשר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the original part or the new growth decide the status of such produce for מעשר?

steps.title: What case is רבה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the exact case is and starts to describe it. The description continues in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? For example...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for the exact case behind רבה's question and begins to spell it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the question can be discussed, the גמרא needs a clear case where the original part and the new growth would lead to different results for מעשר. The word כגון shows the case is about to be given.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances? For example, where...
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next עמוד, where the case is described.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case behind רבה's question in Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case in which רבה's question about מעשר would come up.
